title: Scholarship Opportunity Finder
shortDescription: A centralized digital tool that explores a simpler, more student-friendly way to discover and understand lesser-known scholarships, grants, and funding opportunities.
fullDescription: A student-built project exploring a clearer way to discover and understand lesser-known scholarships, grants, and other funding opportunities.
commitment: Approximately 3–5 hours per week during the six-week sprint. The workload may vary by role and week, but project members should be ready to contribute consistently and communicate with their team.
problemHeading: Useful opportunities are spread across too many places.
problem: Finding scholarships, grants, and other funding can be frustrating. Information is scattered across different websites, while some scholarship-search sites feel cluttered, repetitive, or spammy.
approachHeading: A more student-friendly way to look.
approach: The team will explore a centralized digital tool or database that makes opportunities easier to discover and understand. This is not meant to be another giant list: students will help decide how information should be researched, organized, presented, and eventually accessed.
goal: By the end of the sprint, the team should be working toward a usable version that demonstrates how FYM can make scholarship and funding discovery simpler and more student-friendly.

contributionAreas.name: Tech / Development
contributionAreas.description: Help turn the concept into a functioning digital experience. Work could include developing or improving the interface, organizing how opportunity information is handled, connecting parts of the experience, testing functionality, and fixing technical or usability problems.

contributionAreas.name: Research & Data
contributionAreas.description: Research scholarships, grants, and funding from reliable sources. Organize information consistently; check eligibility, deadlines when available, and official application links; and identify what students need when comparing opportunities.

contributionAreas.name: UI / UX Design
contributionAreas.description: Decide how opportunities should be displayed, organize information visually, design screens and layouts, improve mobile usability, and test whether the experience is clear and intuitive.

sprint.name: Research & Understand
sprint.description: Study existing resources and determine what information students actually need.

sprint.name: Plan
sprint.description: Define the first version, organize the information, and divide responsibilities.

sprint.name: Build
sprint.description: Move research, design, and development from planning into execution.

sprint.name: Test
sprint.description: Use the work as a student would and find confusing, missing, or broken pieces.

sprint.name: Improve
sprint.description: Use feedback to strengthen the parts that matter most.

sprint.name: Finish & Publish
sprint.description: Bring the work into a version that can be shared, demonstrated, or published.
